# Parallel bug-fixing session — 2026-08-20/21

Standing instruction: "dispatch subagents with the rebar-debug skill to resolve all open bugs
without a parent", then "continue driving bugs to completion". ~25 agents dispatched.

## Landed

**45 changes merged.** The final stretch: 1980 (snapshot blob sharing), 1989 (live-DC pass-health
returncode), 1990 (fail-closed on unregistered env-read helpers), 1993 (comment dedup key fitted
like the send path), 1994 (compaction sidecars keyed on the canonical store), 1995 (reactivation
cascade), 1997 (access-check client seam resolved at call time), 1998 (absent-string child
oracles), 1999 (fail-closed on stale KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS rows), 2000 (enrichment queue ordered by
soak deadline), 2001 (a rejected input is not an outage), 2002 (optionality gate if-present
guards).

## The dominant finding — twelve instances of ONE shape

A check whose result is indistinguishable from the check never having run. Filed as
`sphinxian-agrarian-snake` (story, missing review criterion) with five shipped-code instances
linked as evidence.

Five in shipped rebar code, all fixed: absent-string oracles blind to a signal-killed child;
pass-health ignoring a returncode; a "convergence" test that re-derived the send path and so
passed green against the very regression it was named for (paid for in 836 duplicate Jira
comments); and both halves of a registry generator where a missing entry was not an error but
INVISIBLE.

Six in throwaway instruments built BY the agents repairing the first five: a kill matrix grepping
`"^FAILED"` against colorized output (reported all 5 mutations surviving); an orphaned sweep whose
truncated log greps identically to a clean one; a STALE log read as the agent's own sweep, five
hours older than the code it claimed to test; two `pgrep` patterns matching their own shells; and
a shell arg-passing bug that applied no patches while reporting all 9 mutations survived.

One in a CI gate: `_optionality.yml` gaining a step whose test file was created in the same
commit, with no if-present guard — six unrelated changes reddened for reasons unrelated to their
content, two of them with no other failure at all.

**Late refinement:** the pattern has a MIRROR. A verification of a signed close reported every
artifact `ABSENT / 0 bytes` — reading as catastrophic loss — because zsh did not word-split an
unquoted variable. The truth was the opposite. The criterion was broadened from "name every world
where this PASSES" to "name every world where this produces ANY definite result". A false alarm is
*more* likely to be believed, because an alarming result feels like diligence rewarded.

Best formulation, from the agent that read its own stale log:
> a log that says "passed" is indistinguishable from a log that says "passed" about different code

And its rule: **if you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence.**

Three times the shape appeared INSIDE work on the shape itself. Calibration should expect the
diagnostic tooling written to detect it to be a live source of instances.

## Filed this session

`anxious-resistant-urson` (P1, gate skew — FIXED and merged), `friendly-enervative-dikkops`
(worktree retirement destroys unpushed ticket events while every diagnostic reports healthy),
`sphinxian-agrarian-snake` (the pattern story), `equivalent-unpacified-loris` (convergence-test
tautology class), `slithery-cosies-acouchi` (checkout-index unbounded while its sibling read-tree
is bounded), `frilly-hotheaded-queenbee` (make amend-msg drops Signed-off-by — the same silent
trailer loss it was built to prevent for Change-Id), `wolflike-chevroned-haddock` (CLOSED),
`tireless-convenable-canvasback`, `aciduric-enhanced-piranha`, `shaggy-crass-bull`,
`freezing-smooth-godwit`, `velvet-prebeloved-discus` (CLOSED), `bemused-painted-worm`.

## Corrections to my own claims — all caught by measurement, mostly by agents

- "undocumented for a MONTH" -> measured **three days**. I had propagated the wrong figure into a
  filed ticket and corrected it there.
- Census "4 of 11 rows" -> **4 of 13**.
- "the size ladder burns a round-trip per rung" -> it burns **exactly one call** and aborts to an
  unsigned INDETERMINATE; the ladder is dead code for that signal. Worse than I claimed. Corrected
  by comment because the completion verifier reads the description AS THE SPEC — a wrong causal
  claim aims the verifier at the wrong evidence.
- "two repairs already landed" for worktree-locality -> **one closed, one still open**.
- Told two agents to hunt an eager import that did not exist; both corrected me. One pointed out
  its diff moved an import INTO a function body — strictly lazier, so it could not have made an
  optional dependency mandatory. I had reasoned from the symptom instead of reading the log, which
  named the cause in one line.
- Raised an alarm about 209 unpushed ticket commits; it was a compare-and-swap race with
  successful recovery, draining normally. Withdrawn without filing.

## Scope discipline — the rule that held

A bug fix RESTORES documented behaviour; it does not widen. Enforced repeatedly and it changed
outcomes: an agent that widened `claim` to accept `blocked` tickets was reverted; another declined
to add a "fit as much as possible" contract to kill a surviving mutant and recorded it as an
equivalent mutant instead; a third proved a mechanism and STOPPED without writing code because the
fix needed a token estimator and a calibration decision — that ticket was re-typed `bug -> story`,
its claim released, and the genuinely bug-sized half split out and fixed.

The cleanest statement came from the reactivation-cascade fix: *"This does not permit anything
previously refused; it only changes what else moves on that edge, and can narrow via the parent's
gate."*

## Operational lessons

- **Host contention is self-inflicted past a point.** Three concurrent full suites took a 6-minute
  sweep to 38 minutes; load hit 54. Runs died at differing points with exit 144 and zero failure
  markers. Agents correctly recorded these rather than retrying to green.
- **`make lint` does NOT run comment-hygiene** — CI-only, so a local exit 0 cannot catch it. Filed.
- **Gerrit's `owner:self` is shared across sessions.** A `SUBMITTABLE` alert means "some session's
  change is green", not yours. Verified ownership before every submit; caught three foreign
  changes.
- **`--ff-only` refuses after Gerrit rebases on submit.** Verify the merged commit carries your
  Change-Id and byte-identical blobs, then reset your OWN worktree. Never the shared checkout.
- **Checkbox ticks are attestation-safe; AC prose edits are not.** An AC-text correction staled a
  review and forced a full re-run before the close would succeed.

## Handoff state

All 10 tickets this session holds carry a handoff comment stating current state and the next
action. Two closes are dispatched to live agents (`anxious-resistant-urson`,
`sainted-regardable-burro`). Four tickets have MERGED changes but **0 ACs ticked** — deliberately
not ticked, because this session did not verify them; each carries a note naming the specific ACs
that need running, with the mutation-check ones flagged as not rubber-stampable. Four have
genuinely open work: `nuclear-calm-heron` (fix UNLANDED while its sibling merged citing it as
done), `unquieting-godsent-mammal` (P1, blocked on an AC-vs-architecture decision, premise
corrected), `grievous-vulgar-sanderling` (bridge incident resolved and re-verified; canary needs
re-checking against live state before closing), `guiltless-supporting-grayling` (census stale after
45 merges — re-measure first).
